name: Laniakea Supercluster
tagline: Our home supercluster — a 520-Mly basin of ~100,000 galaxies converging on the Great Attractor.
history: Laniakea was defined in 2014 not by where galaxies are but by how they move — a 'watershed' boundary drawn around the volume of space whose matter is all flowing toward the same gravitational basin at the Great Attractor. It contains the Virgo Supercluster, the Local Group, and roughly a hundred thousand other galaxies in a vast flattened network of filaments feeding inward like a river system draining to its mouth. It is the largest gravitationally coherent structure we can claim to be inside.
